answer:
HYPOTHESIS — How the symbolic-capital components (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) are characterized on PC1 and distributed on PC2, from a PCA of the 12 forms of capital across 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300–500):

PC1 (30.3% of variance). All three symbolic indicators load POSITIVELY and with similar, moderate magnitude: hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) = +0.30, daggers (ZDolch) = +0.27, house size (Zhausgr) = +0.23. They therefore sit on the same (positive) side of the dominant "general capital-intensity" axis and co-vary with it, but they do not define it alone — PC1 is driven most strongly by copper/gold (+0.41), pottery decoration (+0.38) and depots/hoards (+0.34). In short, the symbolic indicators are embedded in the overall capital signal on PC1, with hatchets/swords contributing slightly more than house size.

PC2 (19.5% of variance; PC1+PC2 ≈ 49.8%). The three are NOT a coherent group on this axis — they are SPLIT. Hatchets/swords (PC2 loading +0.05) and daggers (+0.07) have essentially near-zero loadings, i.e. they are barely expressed on PC2 and sit close to the PC2 origin, so their variation is captured almost entirely by PC1. House size, by contrast, loads distinctly POSITIVE on PC2 (+0.33), aligning it with the monument-size (+0.39), pottery-form (+0.38), amber (+0.44) and axes/celts (+0.47) cluster rather than with the other two symbolic indicators. Thus house size is the symbolic component differentiated along PC2, while hatchets/swords and daggers are not.

Temporal spread (supporting reading): the composite PC2 score of the 39 slices oscillates over time (range ≈ −3.6 to +2.5), with a pronounced negative excursion in the earliest slices (BCE 4300–4100 ≈ −3.6) and positive peaks around BCE 3500–3200 (≈ +2.0 to +2.5) and BCE 1400–1100 (≈ +0.3 to +2.1) — so PC2 tracks long-run swings in the capital portfolio rather than a stable symbolic-capital signature.

SUMMARY: the symbolic-capital components are characterized by moderate, concordant positive loadings on PC1 (all three on the general-capital axis, hatchets/swords ≈ daggers > house size) and a split distribution on PC2 in which only house size is meaningfully expressed (positive, +0.33), while hatchets/swords and daggers have near-zero PC2 loadings.

On PC2 (19.5%; PC1+PC2 ~49.8%) the three are split: hatchets/swords (+0.05) and daggers (+0.07) have near-zero loadings (barely expressed on PC2, variation captured by PC1), whereas house size loads distinctly positive (+0.33), aligning with monument-size (+0.39), pottery-form (+0.38), amber (+0.44) and axes/celts (+0.47). House size is thus the symbolic component differentiated along PC2; hatchets/swords and daggers are not. The composite PC2 score oscillates over time (range ~ -3.6 to +2.5; negative in BCE 4300-4100, positive peaks ~BCE 3500-3200 and ~BCE 1400-1100), so PC2 tracks long-run portfolio swings rather than a stable symbolic-capital signature. payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (39 rows = the 100-yr slices, BCE 4300-500, comma decimal separator); dropped 'group' and 'color' per dataset documentation, leaving the 12 Z-scored capital variables. Data already Z-scored (per-column mean ~0, std ~1); re-standardized to unit variance (ddof=1) and ran a correlation-matrix PCA via eigendecomposition of the 12x12 correlation matrix with numpy (sklearn unavailable), fixing PC sign so the largest-|loading| is positive. Cross-validated eigenvalues/loadings with an independent SVD (identical). Reported eigenvalues, % variance, PC1/PC2 loadings for all 12 vars (emphasis on the 3 symbolic ones) and PC1/PC2 scores of all 39 slices. Caveat: 39 autocorrelated slices for 12 variables makes PC2/higher loadings less stable (bootstrap 5-95% CIs for the PC2 loadings of hatchets/swords and daggers span zero); this does not change the main pattern. Analysis: analysis_pca.py; summary: results_pca.txt.
